item.text: I’m checking for direct 2024 evidence on protest permission and retaliation, then I’ll synthesize the strongest positive and negative items I can support.

Pakistan 2024 peaceful protest allowed Shehbaz Sharif Reuters

item.text:
**Bottom Line**
The 2024 record is strongly negative on 3B.8. I found only thin, localized evidence of Sharif favoring dialogue over coercion in a few disputes. The dominant pattern is the opposite: election shutdowns, protest crackdowns, late-night detentions, anti-protest lawmaking, internet blocks, and intimidation of dissenting actors. Confidence: moderate.

**Accepted Items**
- [PM urges AJK govt, political leadership to resolve issues through dialogue](https://www.radio.gov.pk/12-05-2024/pm-shehbaz-urges-ajk-govt-political-leadership-to-resolve-issues-through-dialogue) | Radio Pakistan | 2024-05-12  
  Claim-level summary: Sharif told party and local leaders in Azad Kashmir to talk with the action committee and resolve the dispute peacefully. This is the best positive item, but it is narrow and does not amount to a general pro-dissent or pro-protest posture.  
  Question IDs: `3B.8`, also `2B.7`, `3B.6`

- [Election-day internet shutdown is a reckless attack on peoples' rights](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/pakistan-election-day-internet-shutdown-is-a-reckless-attack-on-peoples-rights/) | Amnesty International | 2024-02-08  
  Claim-level summary: Amnesty condemned the telecom and mobile internet shutdown as a rights violation during the election period. This is direct evidence of retaliation-capable control that chilled public participation and dissent around Sharif’s ascent.  
  Question IDs: `3B.8`, also `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.5`, `3B.6`

- [Pakistan: the new Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act threatens the right to protest](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/pakistan-the-new-peaceful-assembly-and-public-order-act-threatens-the-right-to-protest/) | Amnesty International | 2024-09-09  
  Claim-level summary: Amnesty said the new law was rushed through and would criminalize peaceful assembly rather than align protest rules with human-rights standards. That is strong evidence against a permissive stance toward peaceful protest and dissent.  
  Question IDs: `3B.8`, also `3B.5`, `3B.6`

- [Pakistan Government Intensifies Crackdown on Political Dissent](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/09/pakistan-government-intensifies-crackdown-political-dissent) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-10-09  
  Claim-level summary: HRW reported over 500 arrests, tear gas, roadblocks, mobile internet cuts, and arrests of people protesting peacefully. This is the clearest evidence that protest was met with retaliation and collective restriction rather than toleration.  
  Question IDs: `3B.8`, also `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.5`, `3B.6`

- [Pakistani police detain two parliamentarians in swoop on ex-PM Khan's party](https://theprint.in/world/pakistani-police-detain-two-parliamentarians-in-swoop-on-ex-pm-khans-party/2260202/) | Reuters / ThePrint | 2024-09-10  
  Claim-level summary: Police detained PTI parliamentarians after a rally demanding Khan’s release. That supports a pattern of selective punishment against political dissent rather than neutral policing.  
  Question IDs: `3B.8`, also `3B.2`, `3B.5`

- [Pakistan: Urgent and transparent investigation needed into deadly crackdown on opposition protesters](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/urgent-and-transparent-investigation-needed-into-deadly-crackdown-on-opposition-protesters/) | Amnesty International | 2024-11-27  
  Claim-level summary: Amnesty said the Islamabad crackdown on PTI protesters involved deaths, mass detentions, mobile internet shutdowns, and a pattern of intolerance for peaceful assembly. This is strong evidence that peaceful protest was not being protected.  
  Question IDs: `3B.8`, also `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.5`, `3B.6`

- [A dangerous digital crackdown](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/12/dangerous-digital-crackdown) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-12-12  
  Claim-level summary: HRW said internet shutdowns and VPN restrictions had become default policing tools to shut down protests and criticism, while a PECA-linked body would expand prosecution powers. This supports a chilling-surveillance and administrative-restriction reading, not a freedom-to-organize reading.  
  Question IDs: `3B.8`, also `3B.5`, `3B.6`

- [Pakistan authorities must end escalating attacks on minority Ahmadiyya community](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/end-escalating-attacks-on-minority-ahmadiyya-community/) | Amnesty International | 2024-06-21  
  Claim-level summary: Amnesty documented arbitrary arrests, police harassment, and orders blocking Ahmadi rites. While this is also a minority-protection issue, it is relevant here because community organization and religious practice were met with punitive restriction.  
  Question IDs: `3B.8`, also `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.5`, `3B.7`

**Search Gap**
I did not find convincing 2024 evidence that Sharif broadly allowed peaceful protest or dissent without retaliation. The only affirmative material I found was narrow and local, while the more reliable reporting points to a pattern of protest crackdowns, internet shutdowns, and selective punishment.
